constraints.note: Brief applied as hard limits: 5 topics, 7 clips (5 full + 2 impact, cap was 8), every RAW cut under 60 s (longest is clip 1 at 56.13 s; the tighten pass only removes time, so no finished short can reach 60 s). Anything that could not be told in under 60 s was not picked (the modem story, the whole payments-narrative tour). Ranks 1 and 2 are the stream itself: his calls ripping on a red day. Rank 3 is the evergreen conviction piece. Ranks 4 and 5 are lower confidence and easy to kill: rank 4 has him saying 'I hate Ethereum', rank 5 is market talk that the doctrine would normally drop and is in ONLY because Mike recorded the IPO discussion as a miss at the 4b gate of batch peach. Membership pitches, the creator call-outs, the political chat comment and the personal modem tangent are out; there was no ElizaOS talk in this stream. Both impact clips are built from footage their full clip does not use, because past impact cuts that were only a trim of the full got killed. One slot was left unused.

topics.hook_summary: If you got into Pieverse when I called it earlier this year, you'd be up over 17x. My bot called it at a 20 million market cap, I bought it down in here, and now it's like 1.05 billion: divide it by 60 and that's a 17.5. Holy guacamole.

The entire market is dumping, this entire page has only three green bubbles out of 100, and Pippin is ripping again, Velvet is pumping again. All these plays in my community are pumping, everybody else is dumping.

If you have a robot in your house and it has to do a plumbing job, it's going to be an interesting future, and it's going to be tough. You have to invest in assets: it's going to be crazy hard to get ahead if you don't have assets. Stuck on UBI, how the hell are you going to progress?
I even believe, I kid you not, that one day Ethereum is going to flip Bitcoin. I hate ETH, but I got to go where the money is.

topics.hook_type: data-anchored macro take (in on a recorded miss)
topics.hook_summary: This was the SpaceX IPO, and now this is the Anthropic IPO, all this money rotating out. After SpaceX it was a few more weeks before it actually bottomed. We'll take it as it comes: we've got a few plays pumping on a day like this.

clips.title: Pieverse Just Hit a Billion. That Is 17.5x From My Call

segments.why: HOOK, cold, names the coin and the number: 'you got into Pieverse when I called it earlier this year, you'd be up over 17x, man.' Starts in the silence after his false start 'if you got, if', so the leading 'if' is not in the cut.
The call, on the all-time chart: 'Holy guacamole. Look at that, and I called it way back over here. My bot, my bot called it at a 20 million market cap. It started shooting off these messages.'

The entry story as a quoted thought: 'It started going up like, eh, I don't know, it looks pretty good, I don't want to buy it because it's going up. Then it came down a little, and I bought it down in here. I bought it down in here. And then look what happened, and we're doing this right now. Holy guacamole, dude.'

PAYOFF, the math live on the calculator: 'so it's like 1.05 billion, right? So let's do like this, and then we divide it by 60 because it was 60 million market cap. So is that a 17.5? Holy guacamole, dude.' Ends before 'my god' and before the half-the-price community line.

peak_beats.note: 'So is that a 17.5? Holy guacamole, dude.'

clips.notes: Emotional core is segment 3 (the calculator reveal, he reads the 17.5 off the screen and reacts) with segment 2 as the story. Assembly is hook, call, entry, proof, NOT chronological: the hook is from 41:41, the story from 02:49, the math from 06:32. Raw 56.13 s; expect about 45 s after tighten: segment 0 has two 1.2-1.4 s pauses, segment 2 three pauses of about 1 s, segment 3 a 2 s typing pause inside '1 ... .05 billion' and 1.8 s before the reaction. Segment 2 starts on a short dip between 'right?' and 'It started' (not full silence, he runs on), so check that join by ear. The 20 million (bot alert) and the 60 million (where he bought, used in the math) are both his numbers and both stay.

Play one: 'Pippin. Remember Pippin was ripping, we did an 89x at the beginning of this year. Pippin was freaking ripping and suddenly he's ripping again.'
Play two: 'Another one of my plays is pumping, Velvet. We did that 68x on it. And then there was a 58x in June, just a few months back, and this thing is pumping again.'
The joke: 'it knows that I'm going live and it's going up.'

CLOSE, tribal: 'all these plays in my community are pumping, everybody else is dumping, man. Holy crap. And that's why CodeMonkey Mike has the greatest crypto community on the planet. Hell yeah, man.'

peak_beats.note: 'all these plays in my community are pumping, everybody else is dumping ... the greatest crypto community on the planet. Hell yeah, man.'

clips.notes: Emotional core is segment 4 (the brag, delivered right after he sees Velvet up again); segment 3 is the laugh. Scatter-gather across 01:55, 07:05, 14:32 and 15:13; segments 3 and 4 are swapped against stream order so the short ends on 'hell yeah, man'. Raw 54.05 s. Pieverse is deliberately NOT in this clip (it has clips 1 and 6). Same family as peach clip 2 ('Everything Is Low Right Now. These Calls Are Still Up'), which was kept. If it runs long at review, drop segment 3 first.

clips.title: It Will Be Crazy Hard to Get Ahead If You Don't Have Assets

segments.why: HOOK, the picture: 'If you have a robot in your house and it has to do a repair, has to do a plumbing job or has to go out onto the roof or something, it's going to have to order parts and it's going to have to pay things. Man, it's going to be an interesting future, man. It's going to be tough, though.'

THESIS and close: 'you have to invest in assets, because we're going to see an asset-driven future, where you earn dividends off what you own. And it's going to be crazy hard to get ahead if you don't have assets ... you can't get a job and you'll be stuck on UBI, how the hell are you going to progress? That's why anybody watching this channel now, you're on the right path, man. You're not checked out.'

peak_beats.note: 'crazy hard to get ahead if you don't have assets ... stuck on UBI, how the hell are you going to progress?'
'you're on the right path, man. You're not checked out.'

clips.notes: Emotional core is segment 1 from 'crazy hard to get ahead' through the UBI line; the close talks straight at the viewer. Two contiguous passages in stream order (26:11 and 27:11), both in and out points in full silence. Raw 48.89 s; segment 1 has four pauses of about 1 s for tighten. Evergreen, no market state in it. This thesis has been kept every time it was proposed (batches 30x-tao, aliens, best-time, kcc20-live), so it is a safe pick, but it is also the fifth telling: if it feels like a repeat, that is the reason to kill it. What is new here is the robot-in-your-house open. If Mike wants the jobs link said out loud, 1589.93-1597.20 ('There's going to be a lot of changes and it's already happened. Some of you are not feeling it yet. Some of you are.') fits between the two segments and keeps the raw cut at about 56 s.

clips.title: I Hate ETH, But One Day It Is Going to Flip Bitcoin

The pattern behind it: 'I did the same thing with Litecoin. I was like, I can't believe I'm getting back into Litecoin, because it's that made in America token, it's getting ETFs, and now it has an optional privacy feature ... And Ethereum starts giving me the vibe that Ethereum is going to be totally dominant. And I hate Ethereum. I hate it. I hate it. But then it's okay, I'll buy into it because I know it's gonna pump like crazy.'
CLOSE on a number, from 44:45: 'I think the $20,000 ETH is really conservative in my opinion, 10 years from now.'

peak_beats.note: 'one day Ethereum is going to flip Bitcoin. I hate ETH, but I got to go where the money is.'

clips.notes: Emotional core is segment 0 (the 8 s punch) and the tripled 'I hate it' in segment 1. Hook-first on purpose: the clip opens on the positive thesis (ETH flips Bitcoin, a persona core thesis), and the 'hate' is the contrast, not the point; he is buying. Segment 1 comes from just BEFORE the hook in the stream, so 'I did the same thing with Litecoin' lands as 'I went where the money is there too'. Raw 43.73 s. If the Litecoin lead-in drags, the fallback is segment 0 alone, an 8 s punch. Title and caption must not frame ETH as one of his stacking picks.

What it means, then conviction: 'does that mean that we're going to have a bunch of extra weeks, going here, maybe a little bit further down, the same way this happened over here? Well, it is what it is. We'll take it as it comes, man. I have no problem with it right now, because, like,'

clips.title: AI Codes Better Than Any Engineer. You Can't Be a Code Monkey Anymore

Code monkey is just a term for a geek who likes to sit there and just write code all day. That's where I got that term from. And you can't be a code monkey going forward in the future. You just can't do it. You're going to find yourself unemployed.' Ends on 'unemployed', before the product-engineer advice and the JavaScript-developer line.

peak_beats.note: 'That's where I got that term from. And you can't be a code monkey going forward ... You're going to find yourself unemployed.'

review_callouts: Energy is NOT confirmed on any clip: selection is from the transcript only. Clips 1, 2 and 6 read as real excitement on the page ('Holy guacamole', 'hell yeah, man'); confirm by ear on clips 3, 5 and 7, which are calmer talk.

Clip 5 (IPO) breaks the usual no-market-talk rule on purpose, because the peach 4b gate recorded the IPO discussion as a miss. If that note was about peach only, kill clip 5; nothing else depends on it. Also confirm the facts before it ships: that the Anthropic IPO is the event he means, and the chart point he calls the SpaceX IPO.

Clip 4 has him say 'I hate Ethereum. I hate it. I hate it.' The shorts rule is no clip whose core is negative about a named project. I read the core as bullish (he buys it, calls a $20,000 ETH conservative and says it flips Bitcoin), and the clip opens on that claim. Mike's call.

Clip 6 ends on 'probably another 10x on top of where it is right now ... could turn into like 170x'. In the same stream (04:53-05:10) he says getting in after this pump is 'very dangerous, I wouldn't do it'. Clip 1 only looks back at the call; clip 6 is the forward-looking one. Decide if the forward claim should ship without the caution.
Clip 1: the bot alert is at a 20 million market cap and the math divides by 60 (million, where he bought). Both are in the cut. The title uses 17.5x, his own result.

Clip 2: confirm the Velvet numbers. He says 'that 68x' and then 'a 58x in June'; a minute later (15:46) he points at the chart and says 'that 58x'. Captions should show what he says; the title leaves the multiples out for this reason. The 'greatest crypto community on the planet' line also sat in an impact cut that was killed in batch ready-for-pumps.

Clip 7 (code monkey) has a mixed record: 'Even Anthropic's Engineers Say AI Codes Better Than Them' was kept in batch kcc20-live, 'Nobody Is Writing Code Anymore. Every Job Is Next' was killed in batch best-time with no reason on record. It is here for the name-origin line, which is new. If AI-coding talk is not wanted on the crypto channel, kill clip 7; clip 3 stands on its own.

Cut points: Whisper word times drift by up to 1 s in this file, so every in and out point was placed on the silence measured on the master (burst_profile.py; the mic is gated), not on the word times. Two points are NOT in silence because he runs on: clip 1 segment 2 in (182.93) and clip 6 segment 2 out (2530.11). Three more sit in very thin gaps of 50-80 ms: clip 1 segment 3 in (392.84), clip 5 segment 0 out (733.37) and clip 7 out (1739.17). Listen to those five joins.
Clips 1 and 5 lean on the screen (the Pieverse all-time chart and calculator; the Bitcoin chart with his arrows). The picture was not checked: confirm the content zone reads on the vertical.
